ai.description: The Himalayan Keelback reaches 60–90 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow nuchal collar and dark-edged scales. Key features include keeled dorsal scales and a dark streak behind each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Himalayan Keelback is best identified by the distinct, broad, dark V-shaped or chevron mark on the nape, which contrasts sharply with its olive-brown body.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Keelback inhabits moist, temperate forests and rocky stream banks across the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Keelback is primarily diurnal, often foraging for small fish and amphibians along the rocky edges of mountain streams and damp forest floors.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Himalayan Keelback is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–9 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Keelback occurs across the Western and Eastern Himalayas, ranging from Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh at elevations of 1,000–3,000 meters.
